fact_text: Meezan Bank received its commercial banking licence in 2002 as Pakistan's first Islamic commercial bank, according to founder Irfan Siddiqui's account.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: The State Bank governor, Dr Irshad Hussain, granted the licence within about a day after the president approved it, Siddiqui said; the governor called it the last chance to introduce Islamic banking.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Meezan acquired Societe Generale Pakistan in 2002, which brought four branches into the bank; Meezan had six branches at the end of 2002.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Meezan's first branch on a main road was in Gulshan Iqbal, Karachi; earlier branches sat inside buildings and hotels, so the bank was not visible to the public.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Al-Meezan Investment Bank began operating in 1997 and was converted into a full commercial bank in 2002, as the founder described it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Founder Irfan Siddiqui collected PKR 900 million from investors in 1994 to start the Islamic bank project.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: In 1993 Siddiqui met Mufti Taqi Usmani, who explained the Shariah rules on interest-based finance; this led the founders to decide to build an Islamic bank rather than leave the sector.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Irfan Siddiqui, a chartered accountant qualified in England, returned to Pakistan in 1990 to be near his parents and joined Pak-Kuwait Investment Company as general manager.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Siddiqui argued an Islamic investment bank alone is not viable, because finance is a scale business and a bank must take deposits to leverage its capital; a commercial licence was the turning point.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Meezan's branch network grew from six branches in 2002 to 1,083 at publication.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Meezan had about PKR 3,300 billion in deposits and a 9% share of the banking sector at publication.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: The video put Meezan's market value at about USD 3 billion, placing it in the top five group of the Pakistan stock market.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Meezan recorded a record 2025 profit of PKR 92 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Siddiqui received the Outstanding Leader in Islamic Finance award from Global Islamic Finance in 2023.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Meezan was the smallest bank in Pakistan in 2002 and is counted among the country's big five banks at publication.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: The video described Meezan's culture as humble and growth-focused, where staff are encouraged to reach their potential rather than fear colleagues overtaking them.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: Conventional Pakistani banks run Islamic windows; the reporter said these are built on the groundwork Meezan laid.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)

fact_text: The reporter said building public trust in Islamic banking was the sector's biggest challenge, because earlier Islamic-branded banking had not earned it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Irfan Siddiqui: The Man Who Built Pakistan’s Islamic Banking | Founder Stories | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-16)
